ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF HULU SUNGAI SELATAN REGENCY
NUMBER 12 OF 2021
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
Women and Children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of Violence from their families and environment. Various acts of Violence both against women and Children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, Society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency is obligated to provide Protection to women and Children victims of acts of Violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and Children from acts of Violence is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of Regional Regulations as stipulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency has taken steps as efforts to provide Protection to women and Children, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate Protection against acts of Violence that occur in the social life of Society particularly to women and Children, among others caused by the still low understanding of Society regarding the rights of women and Children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable, and so forth. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the Protection of women and Children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from Prevention of acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and Society. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and the participation of the business community and Society, it is hoped that violence against women and Children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from Hulu Sungai Selatan Regency.

6.2.rationale: The Indonesian regulation explicitly includes trafficking within the scope of violence addressed and thus covers trafficking victims under its protection framework. Pasal 3 huruf a states the objective is to prevent violence against women and children "termasuk perdagangan orang" (including trafficking). Pasal 1 angka 13 defines "Perdagangan Orang" (trafficking). Because the regulation’s services/rights (e.g., Pasal 9 on legal protection; Pasal 10 on recovery; Pasal 18 on victims’ rights) apply to "korban tindak kekerasan" and the regulation’s stated objectives explicitly include trafficking, trafficking victims are encompassed as a covered victim group. The judge required trafficking-specific measures distinct from general victim protections, but the indicator (as reflected by the golden label 'Yes') appears to be about whether trafficking victims are addressed/covered at all; the policy does. The retrieved passages already included Pasal 3 and the trafficking definition, so a 'Yes' is supportable from the text; thus the golden label 'Yes' seems correct and the pipeline 'No' is best explained by an overly strict interpretation by the judge.

6.5.rationale: The original Indonesian text does contain a disability/special-needs provision: Pasal 20 states that fulfillment of rights for child victims "yang berkebutuhan khusus" must be handled by the Regional Government and community according to service standards for children with special needs. This is a targeted measure for children with disabilities/special needs. The retrieved English passage (Article 20) reflects this accurately, and the judge used it to answer 'Yes'. If the intended indicator 'Disability' requires explicit measures for persons with disabilities generally (including adult women), then the policy only addresses children with special needs, not women with disabilities; in that case the correct label would be 'No'. The discrepancy is therefore driven by the judge overgeneralizing a child-specific special-needs clause to all persons with disabilities, i.e., a reasoning/threshold error rather than missing evidence.
